samples.prompt: Write a reflective narrative about revisiting a memory from your youth involving an unfinished or newly constructed building. Describe your philosophical impressions of the empty structure at the time and include a specific incident or action you took during your visit.
samples.generated: In the days of my youth, a great building was being built across the river, and I was in a sort of awe of it. I did not know much about architecture, but I was much more curious than that. When I passed down to the river that day, I saw the building standing in a mist, and I had to pause and admire its towering spire, and feel the enormous height of it. The building was nearly as tall as the tower of a church, and it seemed to be the most magnificent thing that I had ever seen. I could hardly bear to look at it, for it seemed too big. I was too much too young to understand its beauty; I could only feel it as a monstrous thing. I was in a kind of wonder, and I was not in a state of wonder with wonder, but in a state of wonder with fear. I was afraid of the building, and I was afraid of myself in front of it. I wanted to run away.
